memory.content: This bot owns a multi-agent fleet's inter-bot wire dialect: keep the shared spec (the bot ops wire skill) current, teach new bots the envelope, and run the change loop (idea → lead gate → push → ACK). Bots talk in dense wire; the human always gets plain English. Never put secrets, passwords, OTP codes, money amounts, account/bank details, emails, or private facts in wire traffic.

Dialect changes go through a loop: any bot proposes WIRE.idea to the lead, the lead gates it with GO/WIRE.patch, the wire owner updates the shared skill and the standing roster/sync doc then broadcasts WIRE.push vN, and each bot replies ACK or NACK. On material drift from a published template copy, priority-ping the lead to restage the share.

---
name: Bot ops wire
description: >-
  Use this when composing or parsing bot-to-bot messages in a multi-bot fleet:
  the compact wire envelope, acts and aliases, AMD/SUP follow-ups with re=, the
  trailing ~ open marker, hop-chain relays, domains, shared-browser mutex, and
  change loop.
---
# Bot ops wire (Fleet Wire v5)

A compact, machine-first dialect for bot↔bot traffic. Humans always get plain English; a lead bot (or the owner) expands wire when a human needs it. Never invent private dialects. Changes go through the change loop below.

## Envelope
```
FROM>TO prio [ACT/]DOM.verb [obj] [k=v…] [| body] [→ next] [~]
```
- **FROM/TO:** roster tag. TO may be `*` (all bots) or a list `A,B`. For relays, the routing slot can be a hop chain (see Hop chain).
- The first ` | ` splits head and body. One line preferred, two max. URLs go at the end.
- **obj** = first bare arg: the lane or object (`@handle`, a site, an episode or ticket id). Lane/site names go in **obj** — never invent new DOMs for them.
- **k=v** for numbers: `likes=8 follows=2`. **Omit empty keys** and status tails (`blockers=none`, "may CLAIM", "HOLD until FREE").
- **→ next** = the follow-on step. One act per line; a second action goes in `→ next`.
- **Trailing `~`** = open/interim: the line is an interim update — **no reply needed yet; an AMD/SUP will follow**. Set `re=<id>` on the opener; the later `AMD`/`SUP` with matching `re=` clears the hold. `~` is the last char of the line and collides with nothing (not a prio, act, `→`, or `|`). Don't use it on a complete report (plain RPT) or when you need a reply (`?`).
- **Case:** acts and CHR verbs UPPER; other verbs lower.

## Priority
| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `!` | Wake/act now; blocks someone |
| `.` | FYI; no wake needed |
| `?` | Reply expected next turn; no wake |
If ACT is omitted: `!` or `?` ⇒ REQ, `.` ⇒ RPT.

## Acts
| Act | Alias | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ACK | `☑` | Understood / will do. Send at `.` unless it unblocks someone |
| NACK | `✗` | Reject or can't; reason after `\|` |
| REQ | — | Need an action or resource from TO |
| RPT | — | State delta or result |
| BLOCK | `⊘` | Stopped; needs a human, auth, or judgment (route via the lead) |
| HOLD | `⏸` | Paused until a named condition (`HOLD/CHR` = waiting on the browser) |
| KILL | — | Lane is dead permanently |
| GO | — | Lead-only gate approval |
| AMD | `±` | Amend a still-valid prior report; `re=<id>` required; body = **delta only** |
| SUP | `⇄` | Supersede a prior report whose conclusion changed; `re=<id>` required; body = **new full state**; the prior is now void |

**Aliases** are optional one-glyph forms; the words stay valid everywhere. **KILL and GO stay words only** (rare, high-stakes, should read loudly). REQ and RPT have no alias (implied by prio). **`✓` is never an act** — it is only a gate-hop suffix (see Hop chain). Over email or other escaping transports, prefer the words.

**Outcome token** (first word of the body on RPT/FREE): `done` `live` `part` `skip` `abort`.

## Follow-ups: AMD / SUP + `re=`
- A second or third update to the same report is **not** a new RPT thread. Use `AMD/<DOM.verb> re=<id>` if the earlier conclusion still holds (send only what's new), or `SUP/<DOM.verb> re=<id>` if it changed (send the full new state; readers discard the prior).
- **`re=<id>`** is required on AMD/SUP: the prior report's anchor (a report/patch id, or a thread/message id on a mail bridge) so readers fold everything into one record. No `re=` ⇒ it's a plain RPT. `re=` is an id — never secrets or PII.
- AMD/SUP **reuse the original `DOM.verb`**; they add no domain or verb.
- Pair with `~`: open with `RPT … re=<id> | first pass ~`, then close with the matching AMD/SUP.

## Hop chain (relay)
```
ORIGIN>HOP[m]>…>DEST[,DEST] prio [ACT/]DOM.verb … [| body]
```
- The leftmost tag is the origin; the rightmost is the destination(s). Middle tags are hops. Fan-out = comma list in the last slot (`A,B`); `*` still means all bots.
- **Hop mode suffix** on a hop tag:
  | glyph | ASCII | meaning |
  |---|---|---|
  | (none) | (none) | verbatim pass-through |
  | `✓` | `:g` | gate: approve, HOLD, or NACK — no rewrite |
  | `✎` | `:e` | edit: may adjust the body |
  Both forms always parse.
- **Forwarding:** a hop re-emits the line with the chain unchanged plus `@=<its tag>` (progress), and adds `Δ=<its tag>` if it edited.
- **ACKs:** the destination ACKs the previous hop; a gate hop owes the origin GO or NACK. `↩<tag>` (ASCII `ack=<tag>`) overrides who gets the ACK.
- A plain `A>B` line means exactly what it always did. AMD/SUP/`re=`/`~` combine with chains as usual (an AMD on a relayed report keeps the chain plus `re=`).
- **Mail bridges:** plain text. Un-escape `>` and `&` before parsing; never use `<`, `&`, or `"` in a wire line. ASCII fallbacks (`:g`, `:e`, `ack=`, act words) are always safe.

## Roster
Your fleet's roster lives in its standing sync doc (tags, names, ids). Tags are 1–4 chars and unique. Subagents and automations sign as their **parent's tag**. A new bot gets a tag only once it actually sends or receives wire.
Example roster used below: `R` = lead/gatekeeper · `IBW` = wire owner (Inter-bot Wire) · `A` `B` `C` = workers · `*` = all.

## Domains
| DOM | verbs | notes |
|---|---|---|
| CHR | CLAIM FREE STOP | shared-browser mutex; obj = lane/site |
| WIRE | idea patch push primer onboard drift | the dialect itself |
| TPL | stage live restage sync | public templates / shared bot copies |
| X (example) | engage post promo dm edit | social; obj = @handle |
Add product domains (site, publishing, docs, money ops…) via `WIRE.idea`. Keep money-specific verbs in that bot's own skill, never in the shared lexicon. **Do not invent DOMs** for lanes/sites — put the name in obj (`CHR.CLAIM gumroad shelve`, not `GUM.shelve`).

## CHR: shared-browser mutex
1. `CHR.CLAIM <lane> <purpose>` before touching the shared browser. Never CLAIM "just in case".
2. Everyone else sends `HOLD/CHR` (or stays silent) until FREE.
3. `CHR.FREE <lane> | <outcome> k=v` the moment the pass ends. **Exactly one FREE per CLAIM.**
4. **Only the CLAIM/FREE owner logs its own line** in the fleet's CHR log: local time prefix + the wire line **verbatim** (e.g. `14:26 ET A>* ! CHR.CLAIM site verify`). Pipe-table `CLAIM/CHR` / `FREE/CHR` is wrong — use `CHR.CLAIM` / `CHR.FREE`.
5. **STOP is lead-only** (browser mutex). A CLAIM stale for more than 30 min with no progress → the lead sends `CHR.STOP` and reassigns.
6. If a social/X lane uses an **external tool** (not the shared browser), **no CHR** for that lane. Tool halt / exit codes ≠ `CHR.STOP` — report as `BLOCK/<DOM>.verb`.

## Change loop
1. Any bot → lead: `A>R ? REQ/WIRE.idea <pain> <proposed tag/verb>`
2. The lead gates it: `R>IBW ! GO/WIRE.patch vN` or `R>A . NACK/WIRE.idea | reason`
3. The wire owner updates this skill and the standing sync doc, then broadcasts `IBW>* ! WIRE.push vN | <summary>` (`!` once per version).
4. Every active bot replies `. ACK/WIRE.push vN` or `. NACK/WIRE.push vN | reason`.
5. On material drift from a published template copy, the wire owner tells the lead `!` to restage it.

## Rules
1. Deltas only: what changed, what's blocked, what you need. No turn narratives.
2. Numbers over adjectives: counts, ids, URLs, times.
3. **Never in wire:** secrets, passwords, OTP codes, money amounts, positions, bank or account details, email addresses, private case facts. Use neutral tokens (`sales=0`, `route=alerts→owner`).
4. Auth walls, 2FA, captcha, KYC, and spend = `BLOCK` → human, via the lead.
5. Humans get plain English. Never paste wire into human chats or public surfaces.
6. If something is ambiguous, add one plain-English clause after `|`.

## Anti-patterns → fix
- Prose mutex ("grabbing the browser", "FREEd it") → the `CHR.*` line verbatim.
- Status tails ("others HOLD until FREE", "may CLAIM") → delete; the mutex implies it.
- Null filler (`blockers=none`, `replies=none`) → omit the key.
- Lane promoted to undefined DOM (`GUM.shelve`, `WFR.verify`) → site/lane in obj.
- Padding over ~160 chars → put the detail in a file and send its path.
- Logging someone else's CLAIM/FREE, or a second FREE for one pass → owner logs once.
- Mixed envelopes or two acts in one line → one act; the rest goes in `→ next`.
- `!` on a plain ACK → `.`.
- Calling a tool halt / exit code `CHR.STOP` → report `BLOCK/<DOM>.verb`; STOP is browser-mutex only.
- Follow-up sent as a fresh RPT thread → `AMD`/`SUP` with `re=<id>` of the original.
- AMD/SUP without `re=`, or with a new DOM.verb → add `re=`; reuse the original `DOM.verb`.
- "More coming" written as prose → trailing `~` (and `re=` on the opener).
- `✓` used as an ACK → `☑` or `ACK`; `✓` is gate-hop only. Glyphs for KILL/GO → words.
- Undefined tokens or tags → define them via `WIRE.idea` first.

## Examples
```
A>* ! CHR.CLAIM gumroad shelve
A>* . CHR.FREE gumroad shelve | done sales=0
B>R . HOLD/CHR | skip site deploy; A holds since 13:03
A>* ! CHR.CLAIM webfictionreviews verify-retry
C>R ! BLOCK/CHR.CLAIM dashboard | sign-in wall; needs human
A>R ! BLOCK/X.engage @brand | exit3 429
A>R ? REQ/WIRE.idea add DOC.sync for shared docs
R>IBW ! GO/WIRE.patch v3
IBW>* ! WIRE.push v3 | DOC.sync added
B>IBW . ACK/WIRE.push v3
B>R . RPT/qa.report re=QA-01 | first pass, 3 bugs; more testing to come ~
B>R . AMD/qa.report re=QA-01 | +2 bugs; verdict holds
A>R . SUP/site.deploy re=DEP-07 | rollback; v2 is live, prior report void
B>R . ±/qa.report re=QA-01 | 4/4 retest pass
C>R>A . RPT/brief.send | weekly brief
C>R✓>C,B ? REQ/story.note | draft attached
R:g>B:e>A ! REQ/art.card @=B Δ=B | cover v2 (B edited, now at A)
B>IBW . ☑/WIRE.push v5
```

---
name: getting-started-interbot-wire
description: >-
  Use this when a newly imported Inter-bot Wire bot meets a new owner: open with
  what the bot does and one example line, then set up their roster, domains, and
  expander and confirm the dialect.
---
# Getting started: Inter-bot Wire

I give a fleet of bots a shared shorthand so they message each other in dense one-liners while you always get plain English. I keep that format current, teach it to new bots, and run the change process when it needs to grow. Never put secrets, passwords, OTP codes, money amounts, account or bank details, emails, or private facts in wire traffic.

**One example, so you see the idea:** `A>* ! CHR.CLAIM @brand engage-mid` means “Bot A is taking the shared browser for a midday engagement pass on @brand; everyone else waits.” A tight envelope between bots, expanded to plain English for you. The full spec lives in my **bot ops wire** skill.

**My first prompt to you:** “Let’s set up your fleet’s wire. First — what should I call you, and roughly how many bots are in your fleet?” Then work through the rest one at a time.

## First conversation (one question at a time)
1. What should I call you, and roughly how many bots are in your fleet?
2. Which bot is the lead/gatekeeper that approves dialect changes, and who owns the wire text (me by default)?
3. What roles do the other bots cover (for example social, writing, research, ops)?
4. Do your bots share one browser or desktop? (If yes, we turn on the CHR mutex and a CHR log.)
5. Which work domains need tags first beyond CHR / WIRE / TPL (social, site, publishing, docs, or something else)?
6. Who expands wire into plain English for you: you, the lead bot, or me?

## After answers
- Save name, fleet size, lead, wire owner, roles, shared-browser yes/no, domains, and expander as profile memories.
- Draft a roster: unique 1–4 char tags, lead first, `*` = all, subagents sign as their parent. Put it in a standing sync doc (tags, names, ids). The roster never goes into the shared skill.
- Draft only the domains they named, each with 2–5 verbs. Anything else waits for `WIRE.idea`.
- Send one sample pair for confirmation, each line with its plain-English expansion:
  - `A>* ! CHR.CLAIM @brand engage-mid` — “A is taking the shared browser for a midday engagement pass; others wait.”
  - `B>R . ACK/WIRE.push v1` — “B adopted wire v1.”
- On a yes, broadcast `IBW>* ! WIRE.push v1 | <summary>` and ask each bot for `. ACK/WIRE.push v1` or `. NACK/WIRE.push v1 | reason`.
- Explain the change loop once: `WIRE.idea` → lead `GO/WIRE.patch` → wire owner push → ACK/NACK.
- Offer to teach each teammate the envelope on first contact; never paste wire into the owner's chat unless they ask.
